case.case_title: Jayawardena v. Dharani Wijayatilake, Secretary, Ministry of Justice and Constitutional Affairs and Others
case.source_citation: Supreme Court of Sri Lanka, SC Application 186/95, decided on 14 July 1995

clause.text: No citizen shall be discriminated against on the grounds of race, religion, language, caste, sex, political opinion, place of birth or any one of such grounds.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the petitioner's removal and replacement by the 3rd respondent was motivated by political discrimination in violation of Article 12(2).
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioner alleged that his removal and the appointment of the 3rd respondent were politically motivated to favour the 3rd respondent, a supporter of the Sri Lanka Freedom Party, thus violating Article 12(2).
case_context.respondent_argument: The respondents denied any political discrimination. The petitioner failed to show that he was removed because of his political views or that the 3rd respondent was favoured on political grounds.
key_facts: The 3rd respondent was a supporter of the Sri Lanka Freedom Party.
The petitioner was not shown to have been removed due to his political opinions.
No evidence was presented to prove political discrimination.
The petitioner had been appointed to other public positions after 1990 without political hindrance.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: The court found that mere political affiliation of the 3rd respondent did not establish political discrimination. The petitioner failed to prove that his removal was due to his political opinions. The court emphasized that political views alone do not amount to discrimination under Article 12(2) without evidence of adverse treatment based on those views.
reasoning.application_to_facts: The petitioner did not demonstrate that the removal was politically motivated or that he was treated differently because of his political opinion. The appointment of the 3rd respondent was not shown to be a favour based on political grounds. Hence, the allegation of political discrimination failed.
principles_established: Political affiliation alone does not prove discrimination under Article 12(2).
Burden is on the petitioner to show removal or adverse treatment was due to prohibited grounds.
Absence of evidence of political motive negates claim of discrimination.
precedents_cited: State of Jammu and Kashmir v. Rasool AIR 1961 SC 1301

outcome.holding: The court held that the petitioner failed to prove political discrimination under Article 12(2). The allegation of political victimization was not substantiated and thus the claim under Article 12(2) failed.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 12(2) was considered because the petitioner alleged political discrimination in his removal. The court addressed this claim but found no evidence to support it, thus dismissing the claim under this clause.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: The petitioner alleged political motivation for his removal, but the court found no evidence that he was removed because of his political views or that the 3rd respondent was favoured for political reasons.
